title: VPC upgrade pipeline: drift-aware migrations and LTS channel rollout gates
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a production-grade VPC/on-prem upgrade pipeline that performs orchestrated, drift-aware migrations with explicit LTS channel gating, cohort canaries, and automated rollback paths. The goal is to enable customers on Private deployments to safely move between LTS and supported channels while preserving data invariants, minimizing downtime, and providing clear operator runbooks and telemetry when rollouts deviate from expected health signals.
background: Customers running Redwood Private ask for predictable LTS upgrades and the ability to opt into newer release channels with strong safety nets. Current ad-hoc upgrade scripts and manual runbooks introduce risk: missed schema migrations, unnoticed state drift, and unclear rollback procedures. We need an upgrade pipeline that understands stateful components (DB schema, object stores, agent versions), runs preflight checks, performs cohort-based canaries, and surfaces failures to Console/Support with actionable remediation steps.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline can run an end-to-end upgrade in a sandbox cluster with simulated stateful workloads and complete all migration hooks without manual intervention
Preflight checks detect incompatible DB schema or agent binary mismatches and block the rollout with remediation guidance
Cohort canary stage can be configured by percentage and region, with automatic pause/rollback on SLO breach or error spike
All upgrade steps and decisions are logged to the audit trail and visible in Console rollout view
A documented runbook for forced rollback and dry-run exists and is validated by a tabletop exercise
tasks: Design migration manifest format (hooks, order, idempotency guarantees)
Implement drift-detection preflight agent (filesystem, DB schema, config diffs)
Add LTS channel pinning and channel-support metadata to release artifacts
Implement cohort canary controller with policy-driven gating based on latency/error metrics
Build rollback orchestration that can reverse stateful changes where possible and mark irreversible steps
Integrate pipeline events with Console rollout view and audit logs
Author runbook and verification tests for on-call and SRE teams
implementation_notes: Prototype will reuse the existing release artifact storage but add a sidecar 'migration-manifest.json' generated at build time. Migration hooks must be idempotent and declare a 'reversible' flag. The canary controller will use Prometheus metrics from the target cluster and the Console trace API for request-level error attribution. For irreversible migrations we will require a manual 'force-approve' step with a human-readable diff in the Console UI.
risks: Irreversible state changes (e.g., destructive schema changes) could require manual remediation if rollback fails
Telemetry blindspots for customer-specific integrations may cause false positives or delayed detection
Network constraints in some customer VPCs could prevent the preflight agent from reporting health status
Regulatory requirements for air-gapped deployments restrict automated rollback options
notes: Initial design review completed 2025-02-18. Security requested an HSM-backed approval token for force-approve flow (security ticket opened). We ran a simulated upgrade against a snapshot cluster; DB migration hook failed due to non-idempotent ALTER statement — conversion needed to a copy/replace pattern. Schedule: implement manifest + preflight agent (2 sprints), canary controller + console integration (2 sprints), rollout validation and runbook (1 sprint).

customer_notes: Planned rollout for early-adopter customers will include manual opt-in. We will provide an RFC to customers describing rollback semantics and a dry-run tool they can execute in their environment. Customers requiring air-gapped upgrades will get a separate signed artifact bundle and offline validation instructions.
qa_plan: Create a matrix of 6 upgrade scenarios (minor, patch, LTS->LTS, LTS->non-LTS, data-migration heavy, network-limited). For each: run dry-run, cohort canary, forced rollback. Capture metrics and automated pass/fail criteria. Add these scenarios to CI with emulated telemetry feeds.
release_notes_draft: Adds a new VPC Upgrade Pipeline with migration manifests, preflight drift detection, cohort canaries, and rollback safeguards. Early-adopter customers can opt into controlled rollouts; irreversible migrations require explicit force approval. Console will display rollout status and audit trail for all upgrade steps.
